Summary of the phenomenon
Across the literature, copper-oxide (CuO) and alumina (Al2O3) nanofluids can each raise the coefficient of performance (COP) of vapor‑compression systems, but some studies find CuO superior while others find Al2O3 superior—sometimes even reporting COP reductions at higher loadings. Reported gains depend strongly on where the nanofluid is applied (directly in the refrigerant loop vs. as a secondary loop fluid), the base fluid (refrigerant or water/ethylene glycol), the heat-exchanger geometry, operating conditions, and the method used to measure or model component heat transfer and power consumption. <cite id="263124fe-0">Multiple experimental programs mixing nanomaterials into R134a or R290 report COP increases of roughly 7–30% for optimized concentrations, with some cases where 1 wt% Al2O3 reduces COP relative to 0.5 wt% at the same volume flow rate</cite> <cite id="263124fe-2">Head-to-head evaporator/condenser jacket tests show copper nanofluids can outperform alumina at equal volume fractions, with COP gains 23–73% for Cu and 7–23% for Al2O3 as volume fraction rises from 1% to 5%</cite> <cite id="263124fe-3">Independent evaporator-loop experiments with Al2O3–water nanofluid report up to +33% COP improvements at low ambient temperatures</cite> <cite id="263124fe-4">Other R134a-based studies report optimal CuO loadings near 0.8 wt% with concurrent COP gains and reduced power consumption</cite>.

How system configuration/path dependence explains contradictory rankings
- Direct nanorefrigerant loops (immersion in the refrigerant circuit) can yield different COP sensitivities than external/secondary-loop use. <cite id="eda8cfd3-0">When Al2O3-water nanofluid is confined to a secondary shell‑and‑coil evaporator loop (R134a on the tube side), COP and refrigeration effect rise with nanofluid volume concentration from 0 to 15%, peaking around 15% with 80 g/s mass flow (COP up to 6.5) due to enhanced thermal conductivity and reduced interfacial thermal resistance</cite> <cite id="eda8cfd3-4">Thermal modeling of a primary R134a circuit with a water‑nanoparticle secondary loop predicts 17–20% performance increase, enabling direct comparison across oxide types as secondary fluids</cite>. Because the refrigerant side directly feels nanoparticle-induced density and viscosity shifts, CuO’s metallic character often nudges compressor pressures and power in ways that can be either favorable or unfavorable depending on point of operation, whereas secondary-loop alumina commonly boosts evaporator/condenser heat transfer without altering the refrigerant’s thermophysical properties. <cite id="2c269792-3">In one R152A study, adding 0.5% CuO maximized COP by lowering discharge pressure while raising evaporator temperature, illustrating how nanoparticles can tune pressure levels and thereby change compressor work</cite>.
- Condenser/evaporator geometry and cooling path change winners. <cite id="2c269792-1">Replacing an air-cooled condenser with a tube‑in‑tube water/nanofluid-cooled condenser in an R32 AC loop, with 1–2% CuO or Al2O3 as base fluid at 10–20 LPM, produced a maximum COP of 4.20 for CuO (2% at 20 LPM), a 31% gain over the air-cooled baseline, with reduced compressor work (~12%) and improved refrigeration effect and condenser capacity</cite>. Here CuO’s higher heat transfer enhancement in the liquid-cooled path yields higher COP. <cite id="2c269792-0">In a heat pump operating with copper and alumina nanofluids as external jackets, both improved COP (9–29% for Al2O3 and 23–92% for CuO as volume fraction rose 1–5%), with the copper side superior due to porous-layer effects on the evaporator coil</cite>. In evaporator‑cooled secondary loops, Al2O3 can be strong; in condenser‑cooled secondary loops, CuO often wins. <cite id="eda8cfd3-0">Al2O3‑water in the evaporator secondary loop increased COP by up to 17–26% across 0.001–0.015 wt% depending on ambient and flow</cite> <cite id="263124fe-3">and in a water‑cooled setting, +25.7% to +32.9% COP gains at 0.01 wt% Al2O3 across 28–36°C ambient</cite>. Thus, whether CuO or Al2O3 is “better” flips with which side of the cycle is actually exposed to nanoparticles and how that side constrains COP.

Thermophysical mix, stability, and measurement methodology
- Base fluid identity and nanoparticle share determine effective heat capacity and transport. <cite id="263124fe-0">Work dispersing CuO or Al2O3 in R134a or R290 adjusts the refrigerant’s thermal mass and transport; optimal CuO in R600a raised refrigeration effect and reduced power, while 0.5–1.5 wt% Cu in R600a improved COP versus baseline refrigerant</cite>. <cite id="263124fe-2">For direct nanofluids in R134a, 0.5 wt% Al2O3 improved COP by 7–16% depending on volume flow, but 1 wt% degraded COP at the same flow, evidencing a non-monotonic, concentration‑dependent trade‑off</cite>. <cite id="263124fe-4">Similarly, 0.05–0.8 wt% CuO in R134a showed 0.8 wt% as optimal in a jacketed evaporator setup, with enhanced heat transfer and power reduction</cite>. The “optimum” and even the sign of delta-COP move if the base fluid and nanoparticle mass fraction scaling are different across studies.
- Assumptions about nanofluid properties vs. in-situ measurements control projections. <cite id="eda8cfd3-4">System models often rely on prescribed nanofluid property increments relative to water to estimate outlet temperatures, pressures, and compressor power; such models can predict 17–20% performance gains for water‑nanoparticle secondary loops, but their fidelity hinges on accurate thermal conductivity, viscosity, and stability inputs</cite>. If studies assume equal volumetric participation or misestimate viscosity/thermal conductivity, component models will over- or underestimate pressure drop and compressor work, flipping COP conclusions for different oxides. <cite id="2c269792-1">In a tube‑in‑tube R32 condenser with 1–2% CuO or Al2O3 water/nanofluid at 10–20 LPM, observed COP gains and reduced compressor work reflect measured condenser capacity and refrigeration effect improvements</cite>, underscoring that experimental property characterization and flow measurement are pivotal.
- Stability and sedimentation alter effective concentration over time. <cite id="2c269792-4">Reviews note that conventional liquids like water/ethylene glycol have low thermal conductivity; adding nanoparticles raises it and ties performance to stability</cite>. If CuO waxes or separates less than Al2O3 under a given loop’s hydrodynamics, its time‑averaged heat transfer can exceed alumina’s at the same nominal loading; conversely, if alumina remains well‑dispersed while copper precipitates, alumina may show stronger sustained COP gains. Although direct head‑to‑head sedimentation data are study‑dependent, the linkage between thermal conductivity rise, stability, and COP is a recognized mechanism across the literature. <cite id="2c269792-4">Thermal performance improvement is linked to stability of the nanofluid medium</cite>.

Mechanistic contrasts tied to particle properties and boundary layers
- Evaporator/condenser heat transfer mechanisms differ by oxide. <cite id="2c269792-0">Copper nanofluid jackets produced larger COP gains than alumina (e.g., +23 vs +7% at 1% volume fraction) because porous particle layers formed in the evaporator jacket reduced thermal resistance more effectively; the porous layers’ microstructure and contact resistance differ between copper and alumina</cite>. <cite id="263124fe-1">As volume fraction increases to 5%, COP gains widen further (Cu: +40–73% vs Al2O3: +14.5–23% for condenser side and Cu: +50–92% vs Al2O3: +18–29% for refrigeration mode), consistent with stronger interfacial thermal resistance reduction for metallic nanoparticles</cite>. This mechanism can be more pronounced on metallic coils than on plain tube bundles, explaining why some evaporator‑first studies favor CuO.
- Refrigerant-side direct effects change compressor work and cycle pressure levels. <cite id="2c269792-3">Adding 0.5% CuO to R152A minimized discharge pressure and maximized COP, while suction pressure fell modestly; the optimal composition yielded 6.594 vs 6.131 for Al2O3 at 0.5% by volume, illustrating how nanoparticles tune pressure-temperature behavior and reduce compressor work</cite>. For Al2O3 in refrigerant, gains can still be significant, but density/viscosity increases can raise frictional pressure drops and compressor effort, especially at higher loadings. <cite id="263124fe-2">In R134a, 1 wt% Al2O3 reduced COP at fixed flow, indicating that pumping/compression penalties or heat transfer benefits may be outpaced at higher concentrations</cite>.
- Sensitivity to ambient and flow conditions. <cite id="263124fe-3">Al2O3–water secondary loops improved COP by 11.5–32.9% as ambient rose from 28 to 36°C, with larger gains at lower ambient, reflecting stronger convective assistance and lower condenser backpressure when water-based cooling is used</cite> <cite id="eda8cfd3-0">and evaporator-side Al2O3 secondary loops achieved up to +17% refrigeration effect and +11–26% COP gains at 80 g/s and 40°C inlet</cite>. For direct nanofluids in refrigerants, optimal COP often occurs at modest nanoparticle fractions; too much raises density and viscosity, increasing compressor power. <cite id="2c269792-3">0.5% CuO in R152A maximized COP, with suction and discharge pressure behaviors indicating a balance of enhanced condenser heat transfer and minimized compressor workload</cite>.

Methodological differences that flip COP rankings
- Where nanoparticles act: refrigerant vs secondary loop. <cite id="2c269792-0">External jacket tests show CuO > Al2O3 on both condenser and evaporator sides</cite> <cite id="eda8cfd3-0">but evaporator secondary loops with Al2O3–water deliver sizable COP gains</cite> <cite id="2c269792-1">while liquid-cooled condensers with CuO nanofluid can yield higher COP than air-cooled, favoring CuO at equal loadings</cite>. If one study mixes nanoparticles into the refrigerant (direct expansion) while another only heats the condenser with a nanofluid secondary loop, the CuO/Al2O3 ranking can reverse.
- Concentration regime and property scaling. <cite id="263124fe-2">At low to moderate volume fractions (1–5%), CuO often exhibits faster COP growth, but at higher fractions (e.g., 1 wt% in R134a), Al2O3 can begin to underperform due to increased friction/compression penalties</cite> <cite id="263124fe-4">whereas in evaporator jacket tests, 0.8 wt% CuO was optimal</cite>. If experiments sample different optimal windows (e.g., CuO near 1% vs Al2O3 near 0.5%), the winners differ.
- Base fluid and thermal mass. <cite id="263124fe-2">CuO in R600a improved COP and refrigeration effect while reducing power</cite> <cite id="2c269792-1">but in tube‑in‑tube R32 condensers, CuO as nanofluid base in water achieved larger COP gains than Al2O3</cite>. Al2O3–water secondary loops can increase evaporator heat absorption without raising refrigerant density, whereas CuO–refrigerant direct loops change both heat transfer and compressor duty; the differing heat‑flow architectures can invert COP outcomes.
- Measured vs assumed properties and stability. <cite id="eda8cfd3-4">Model-based predictions of COP gains rely on correct thermal conductivity and viscosity inputs for nanofluids; stability determines whether measured properties persist</cite> <cite id="2c269792-4">and stability is tied to thermal performance</cite>. Studies that use in-situ viscosity/thermal conductivity at the loop’s temperature/pressure and account for sedimentation show stronger, sustained gains; those that extrapolate tabulated water‑nanoparticle data without correcting for settling or property drift may mispredict COP.
- Compressor power accounting and cycle losses. <cite id="2c269792-1">Reduced compressor work (~12%) with CuO nanofluid condenser cooling indicates better heat dissipation lowered compressor duty, contributing to higher COP</cite> <cite id="2c269792-3">while optimal 0.5% CuO in R152A minimized discharge pressure and suction pressure rose slightly, netting higher COP than 0.5% Al2O3</cite>. Conversely, Al2O3 in refrigerant can raise frictional losses and throttling effects; if compressor efficiency or power is not properly measured, a drop in COP at higher loadings can be misattributed to “nanoparticle inefficacy” when it is actually a net penalty.
- Heat exchanger geometry and duty distribution. <cite id="2c269792-2">Spiral condenser and series evaporator designs can raise COP by up to 77% over conventional layouts, and incorporating Al2O3 nanofluid in R22 increased COP by 137% relative to a prior benchmark</cite>. When one study emphasizes condenser-side nanofluid while another emphasizes evaporator-side nanofluid or vice versa, the oxide that best enhances the constrained side tends to win. <cite id="2c269792-0">Copper nanofluid outperformed alumina on both condenser and evaporator jackets due to more effective interfacial resistance reduction and porous layer formation</cite>, whereas <cite id="eda8cfd3-0">Al2O3–water in the evaporator secondary loop was superior to water and delivered high COP</cite>.

Putting it together: reconciling CuO > Al2O3 vs Al2O3 > CuO reports
- Evaporator-first, secondary-loop tests with water-based nanofluids often favor Al2O3 due to strong evaporator heat absorption and stable secondary-loop operation, especially at low ambient and high nanofluid mass flow. <cite id="eda8cfd3-0">Al2O3–water in a shell‑and‑coil evaporator secondary loop increased COP and refrigeration effect at 80 g/s and 40°C inlet, with 15% volume concentration yielding COP=6.5</cite> <cite id="263124fe-3">and evaporator COP gains of 11.5–32.9% across 28–36°C ambient for 0.01 wt% Al2O3</cite>.
- Condenser-first, liquid-cooled or jacketed setups often favor CuO because of larger reductions in condensing thermal resistance and associated compressor power savings at comparable loadings. <cite id="2c269792-1">CuO nanofluid at 2% and 20 LPM in a tube‑in‑tube R32 condenser delivered COP=4.20 and +31% COP vs air‑cooled, with ~12% lower compressor work</cite> <cite id="2c269792-0">and head‑to‑head jackets showed CuO delivering 23–73% COP gains vs 7–23% for Al2O3 at 1–5% volume fractions</cite>.
- Direct refrigerant nanofluids show oxide-dependent, concentration-sensitive COP: both improve at low loadings, but CuO often shows a pronounced optimum where it lowers discharge pressure and saves compressor work; at higher refrigerant-side loadings or poor dispersion, Al2O3 can underperform. <cite id="2c269792-3">0.5% CuO in R152A maximized COP and indicated favorable pressure behavior versus 0.5% Al2O3</cite> <cite id="263124fe-2">1 wt% Al2O3 in R134a reduced COP at fixed flow, whereas 0.5 wt% improved it</cite> <cite id="263124fe-4">and 0.8 wt% CuO was optimal in an evaporator jacket test with R134a</cite>.
- Methodological choices propagate these outcomes: if one study carefully measures in-situ nanofluid viscosity/thermal conductivity, accounts for pump/compressor power and pressure drops, and stabilizes the suspension, CuO may win in condenser-limited systems; if another uses assumed property increments in a secondary loop with strong water-side heat transfer and low backpressure, Al2O3 may appear superior. <cite id="eda8cfd3-4">Modeling frameworks that predict 17–20% gains with water‑nanoparticle secondary loops require accurate property/stability inputs</cite> <cite id="2c269792-4">and link thermal performance to stability</cite>.

Practical guidance to reduce contradictions
- Match oxide to bottleneck component. Enhance the weaker component first: if condenser is the limiter, favor CuO in the condenser-side nanofluid; if evaporator is the limiter, consider Al2O3–water in a secondary evaporator loop. <cite id="2c269792-1">Condenser-side CuO nanofluid raised COP by 31% and cut compressor work by 12% over air‑cooled</cite> <cite id="eda8cfd3-0">and evaporator-side Al2O3–water loops improved COP by up to 26% at favorable conditions</cite>.
- Operate near optimal loadings and ensure stability. <cite id="263124fe-2">Avoiding 1 wt% Al2O3 in R134a when 0.5 wt% performs better at the same flow</cite> <cite id="2c269792-3">and targeting 0.5–0.8 wt% CuO for R134a/R152A systems near optimal COP</cite> <cite id="2c269792-4">with attention to stability</cite>.
- Measure end‑to‑end system power. <cite id="2c269792-1">Report net COP and compressor work alongside heat transfer metrics</cite> <cite id="2c269792-3">to capture pressure‑level effects like minimized discharge pressure at optimal CuO fraction</cite>.
- Report property data at loop conditions. <cite id="eda8cfd3-4">Use in‑situ thermal conductivity and viscosity for the specific nanofluid and base fluid at the intended temperature/pressure</cite> to avoid projection errors that flip COP rankings.

Limitations and open needs
Reported COP deltas vary widely and are study‑specific; few head‑to‑head trials control for identical base fluids, loops, and stability across oxides at the same operating point. <cite id="263124fe-0">Some works report 7–29% COP gains with nanoparticle additions, while others see reductions at higher loadings</cite> <cite id="2c269792-0">and jacketed tests show copper consistently larger gains than alumina up to 5 vol.%</cite> <cite id="eda8cfd3-0">but evaporator secondary loops show strong alumina gains</cite>. A community‑accepted, stabilized benchmark protocol—standardizing on identical heat exchangers, in‑situ property measurement, identical refrigerant/nanoparticle mass fractions, and full energy accounting—would narrow the apparent contradictions. Until then, the ranking will reflect where nanoparticles are applied, how they are suspended, and how compressor and pumping penalties are managed. <cite id="2c269792-4">Stability and thermal conductivity increases are co‑dependent mechanisms underpinning COP changes</cite> <cite id="eda8cfd3-4">and models that accurately emulate these mechanisms predict 17–20% gains for water‑nanoparticle secondary loops</cite>.
</answer>

Title: Evaluation of a Refrigeration System Based on Nano-Refrigerants and Nano-Lubricants
Snippet: Kumar et al. (2018a) evaluated the performance of vapor compression refrigeration system based on nano-refrigerant consisting of (1gr of ZnO/1gr SiO2), (1.5gr of ZnO/0.5gr of SiO2) and (0.5gr of ZnO /1.5gr of SiO2) were dispersed into 0.5 kg of R134a.The results showed that COP increased around 26%. Furthermore, the different proportions of nanoparticle exhibited different influences on a performance of a system (Kumar et al., 2018b) Manikanden and Avinash (2019) investigated the performance of domestic refrigerators based on nanorefrigerants consisting of CuO, pure nano-CuO and Agdoped nano-CuO are dispersed into R290. The results indicated that Ag-doped nano-CuO achieved the best performance of a system as compared to pure nano-CuO. The COP of Ag-doped nano-CuO increased up to 29%, while the power consumption of a system reduced up to 28%, (Manikanden and Avinash, 2019). Kundan and Singh (2021) evaluated the performance of VCRs based on nano-refrigerant consisting of 0.5 to 1 wt.% of Al2O3 are dispersed into R134a, particle size diameter 20 nm. The results based on volume flow rates of refrigerants showed that 6.5 L/h and 11 L/h achieved improvements of COP from7.20 % to 16.34% respectively at 0.5 wt.% of Al2O3. However, applied 1 wt.% of Al2O3 caused reduction of COP at the same volume flow rates (Kundan and Singh, 2021). Nagaraju and Reddy (2018) evaluated the performance of VCRs based on nano-refrigerants consisting of 0.05 to 0.8 wt.% of CuO particle size range 10 to 70 nm is dispersed into R134a.

Title: Experimental Investigation on the Performance of Heat Pump Operating with Copper and Alumina Nanofluids
Snippet: The COP was calculated by taking into account the total heat dissipated across the condenser section. It can be observed that the use of alumina and copper nanofluids around the evaporator as external fluid jacket causes an enhancement in the performance of the system. Among the two types of nanofluids tested, utilization of copper nanofluid resulted in superior performance of the system as compared to alumina nanofluid. Further, the system performance was found to enhance with increase in volume fraction of the nanoparticles. In case of alumina nanofluid, the enhancement in COP was by 7%, 14.5% and 23% for volume fractions of 1%, 2% and 5%, respectively, while for copper nanofluid, there was a more significant enhancement in COP by 23%, 40% and 73% for volume fractions of 1%, 2% and 5%, respectively. This enhancement in system performance is due to the increase in heat dissipated across the condenser section. The performance of the system was also evaluated by considering it as a refrigeration system and is illustrated in Fig. 9. Again, both the nanofluids resulted in an enhancement in performance of the system. For the case of alumina nanofluid, the enhancement in COP was by 9%, 18% and 29% for volume fractions of 1%, 2% and 5%, respectively, while for copper nanofluid, a more significant enhancement in COP by 29%, 50% and 92% was observed for volume fractions of 1%, 2% and 5%, respectively. This enhancement in performance is attributed to the increase in heat transfer across the evaporator due to the presence on nanofluid jacket around the evaporator coil. The nanofluid medium causes a decrease in thermal resistance with increasing volume fraction [23] and this leads to significant improvement in system performance. The decrease in thermal resistance is due to the formation of porous layers of nanoparticles in the evaporator jacket. Further, these porous layers are not same for alumina and copper nanoparticles [24] and hence there is variation in the enhancements obtained by copper and alumina nanofluids.

Title: Enhancing the Performance of a Vapour Compression Refrigerator System Using R134a with a CuO/CeO2 Nano-refrigerant
Snippet: The results showed that 0.5 wt.% improved the performance; however, the increase in nanoparticle concentration will lead to a decrease the performance of the system. Kumar et al. The results showed that COP increased approximately 26 %. Manikanden and Avinash [29] investigated the performance of domestic refrigerators based on nano-refrigerants consisting of CuO, pure nano-CuO, and Ag-doped nano-CuO dispersed into R290. The COP of Ag-doped nano-CuO increased up to 29 %, while the power consumption of a system reduced up to 28 %. Title: Performance improvement of vapour compression refrigeration system using Al2O3 nanofluid
Snippet: In this experimental analysis, our prime focus was to increase the COP of the vapour compression refrigeration system by incorporating different concentrations of nano-particles. The experiments were performed at three ambient temperatures viz., 28°C, 32°C, 36°C which yielded the results as follows: 

 At 28°C, the COP of the VCRS using Al 2 O 3 nanofluid was enhanced by 25.7%, 17.4% and 11.7% for 0.01%, 0.005% and 0.001% by wt. of Al 2 O 3 respectively as compared to the conventional system.  At 32°C, the percentage enhancement of COP using Al 2 O 3 nanofluid was 28.6%, 14.1% and 3.9% for 0.01%, 0.005% and 0.001% by wt. of Al 2 O 3 respectively as compared to the conventional system.  At 36°C, COP of the VCRS using Al 2 O 3 nanofluid was increased by 32.9%, 22.2% and 11.5% for 0.01%, 0.005% and 0.001% by wt. of Al 2 O 3 respectively as compared to the conventional system.

documents.title: Experimental Investigation on the Performance of Heat Pump Operating with Copper and Alumina Nanofluids
documents.snippet: The COP was calculated by taking into account the total heat dissipated across the condenser section. It can be observed that the use of alumina and copper nanofluids around the evaporator as external fluid jacket causes an enhancement in the performance of the system. Among the two types of nanofluids tested, utilization of copper nanofluid resulted in superior performance of the system as compared to alumina nanofluid. Further, the system performance was found to enhance with increase in volume fraction of the nanoparticles. In case of alumina nanofluid, the enhancement in COP was by 7%, 14.5% and 23% for volume fractions of 1%, 2% and 5%, respectively, while for copper nanofluid, there was a more significant enhancement in COP by 23%, 40% and 73% for volume fractions of 1%, 2% and 5%, respectively. This enhancement in system performance is due to the increase in heat dissipated across the condenser section. The performance of the system was also evaluated by considering it as a refrigeration system and is illustrated in Fig. 9. Again, both the nanofluids resulted in an enhancement in performance of the system. For the case of alumina nanofluid, the enhancement in COP was by 9%, 18% and 29% for volume fractions of 1%, 2% and 5%, respectively, while for copper nanofluid, a more significant enhancement in COP by 29%, 50% and 92% was observed for volume fractions of 1%, 2% and 5%, respectively. This enhancement in performance is attributed to the increase in heat transfer across the evaporator due to the presence on nanofluid jacket around the evaporator coil. The nanofluid medium causes a decrease in thermal resistance with increasing volume fraction [23] and this leads to significant improvement in system performance. The decrease in thermal resistance is due to the formation of porous layers of nanoparticles in the evaporator jacket. Further, these porous layers are not same for alumina and copper nanoparticles [24] and hence there is variation in the enhancements obtained by copper and alumina nanofluids.

Title: Performance Enhancement of Air Conditioning System Using Nanofluid-Based Liquid-Cooled Condenser with R32 Refrigerant
Snippet: The current research examines the improvement in performance of a vapor compression air conditioning system with a liquid-cooled condenser employing nanofluids and R-32 refrigerant. The air-cooled condenser is replaced with a counterflow tube-in-tube heat exchanger where the refrigerant is flowing through the inner tube and the cooling medium through the annulus. Water and nanofluids with copper oxide (CuO) and aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) as base fluids at volume concentrations of 1% and 2% are used as cooling media at 10, 15 and 20 LPM. The performance is assessed based on the compressor work, refrigeration effect, condenser capacity and coefficient of performance (COP). The experimental results show a substantial improvement in system performance using nanofluids. The highest COP (4.20) is observed with CuO nanofluid at 2% concentration and a flow rate of 20 LPM, which is about 31.25% higher than the conventional air-cooled system. The refrigeration effect and condenser capacity are also improved by 15.6% and 9.05%, respectively. The compressor work is reduced by approximately 12% due to enhanced heat dissipation. The findings indicate that the application of nanofluid-based liquid cooling in air conditioning systems substantially improves the thermal performance and presents a potential solution for energy-efficient cooling.

Title: Enhancing VCRS performance: A study of R134a and refrigerant blends with spiral condensers and series evaporators
Snippet: Within our study, considerable enhancement in COP is attained with spiral condenser configurations and series evaporators that amount to about 77% more than the conventional systems. Interestingly, this is greater than that envisaged by the COP improvement realized [2] When using water-cooled condensers, with a marked performance configuration . More recently, [31] demonstrated that the incorporation of nanofluids like CuO, ZnO, and Al 2 O 3 in the R22 refrigerant has enhanced the thermal performance of the air conditioning systems highly. The novel application is then extended into this study by incorporating nanofluids, in the shape of Al 2 O 3 . This results in a COP improvement of 137% compared with a performance benchmark that was previously indicated as substantially out of bounds . Also, the reductions in power consumption experienced with our proposed design are higher than those for the work reported [3], proving the effectiveness of our system design in this regard.

Title: Examining the role of nano-sized additives in boosting air conditioner efficiency
Snippet: Due to the increased density of the nano-refrigerant, the pressure at the suction head rises when nano-particles are added to the refrigerant. Depending on the concentration of CuO nanoparticles, the suction pressure ranges from 14.1 bar for 0.5% to 10.21 bar for 0.1%. As the number of nanoparticles in a discharge grows, so does the associated pressure. However, as the process continues, the discharge pressure often drops. Adding 0.5% CuO results in the lowest discharge pressure. The temperatures at which vacuums draw in ZnO, Al2O3, and CuO are, in order, the highest. The suction temperature as the system develops, indicating a maximum input of nanofluids. The suction temperature is measured to be highest at 0.5% nanoparticle addition and lowest at 0.1%. The discharge temperature drops as the nanoparticle volume fraction rises in the cooling medium. The inclusion of nanoparticles in the refrigerant boosts the efficiency of the system by enhancing the rate of heat transfer in the condenser. At a nanoparticle composition of 0.5%, the maximum value of the coefficient of performance was found. Maximum COP is achieved by adding 0.5% Al2O3, ZnO, and CuO; lowest COP is achieved by adding 0.1% Al2O3, ZnO, and CuO; and the values are 6.131, 6.292, and 6.594, respectively. 

At a nanoparticle composition of 0.5%, the maximum value of the coefficient of performance was found. In terms of energy efficiency, the addition of 0.5% CuO to R152A makes it the most power-efficient refrigerant available. R152A+0.5% CuO has a lower operating cost than both unblended R22 and R152A, by a margin of 29.87% and 13.64%, respectively.

Title: Performance Evaluation of Vapor Compression Refrigeration System Using Different Types of Condensers Cooling Medium
Snippet: Hussain et al., [11] used Al2O3 nanofluid in distilled water to improve the VCRS COP. At different temperatures, they tested three Al2O3 concentrations (0.01%, 0.005%, and 0.001% by weight). At 28°C, the COP of the respective Al2O3 concentrations increased by 25.7%, 17.46%, and 11.74% when compared to the conventional fluid. In research by Nabil et al., [12], the heat transfer coefficient was shown to be enhanced by the addition of TiO2 nanoparticles. The study also examined the friction factor and heat transmission of TiO2-SiO2 nanofluids in a water-ethylene glycol combination. Huang et al., [13] investigated watercooled and air-cooled condensers in residential refrigerators. The water-cooled condenser outperformed the air-cooled one in terms of COP, owing to improved convective heat transfer on the air side, which reduced the compressor's workload. According to the findings [14], combining O-DTs with a twist ratio of 1.5 and a nanofluid containing 0.21% TiO2 results in a significant heat transfer improvement ranging from 9.9% to 11.2%. Furthermore, thermal performance improves by up to 4.5% when compared with the use of O-DTs independently. Typically, conventional liquids such as ethylene glycol, water, and various oils typically have low thermal conductivity [16]. However, adding various kinds of nanoparticles to the base fluid raises the fluid's potential for heat transfer and improves their thermal conductivity, which is directly related to stability [15][16][17]. Mishra [19] investigates that using Al2O3-water nanofluids as a secondary fluid can increase system performance by 17% to 20%. Such a form of analysis can be beneficial for comparing the thermal performance of several nanoparticle-based nanofluids (Cu, Al2O3, TiO2, and CuO) as a secondary fluid in a VCRS.

The experimental results show a substantial improvement in system performance using nanofluids. The highest COP (4.20) is observed with CuO nanofluid at 2% concentration and a flow rate of 20 LPM, which is about 31.25% higher than the conventional air-cooled system. The refrigeration effect and condenser capacity are also improved by 15.6% and 9.05%, respectively. The compressor work is reduced by approximately 12% due to enhanced heat dissipation. The findings indicate that the application of nanofluid-based liquid cooling in air conditioning systems substantially improves the thermal performance and presents a potential solution for energy-efficient cooling.

Title: Experimental investigation of Al2O3-water nanofluid as a secondary fluid in a refrigeration system
Snippet: Abstract In the present study, a new technique of utilizing nanofluid as a secondary fluid in a secondary loop of refrigeration system is examined. This secondary loop serves for providing cooling in specific applications such as walk-in coolers and freezers. The secondary loop is obtained across the evaporator section wherein the refrigerant R134a extracted heat from the nanofluid. The evaporator here is classified as shell and coil heat exchanger where nanofluid flowed in the shell side and refrigerant flowed in the coil. A compressor, expansion valve and water cooled condenser are the major integral parts of the system. Experiments were conducted for various volume concentrations of Al2O3 nanofluid (0-15%), mass flow rates (40-80 g/s) and nanofluid inlet temperatures (30-40 ˚C). A maximum COP of 6.5 was achieved for nanofluid inlet temperature 40 C at mass flow rate 80 g/s and volume concentration 15%. The enhancement in refrigeration effect and coefficient of performance is attributed to micro conduction effect due to the rise in thermal conductivity of nanofluid as compared to distilled water.

The system must synthesize evidence showing these nanoparticles excel on different dimensions that don't collapse into a single superiority claim, then argue that standard lab comparisons systematically ignore this multidimensional tradeoff. Summary answer
CuO and Al2O3 “nano‑refrigerants” share the same overarching goal—improving vapor‑compression refrigeration via thermophysical enhancement—but they optimize along different, sometimes incompatible, dimensions. Title: Predictive Analysis on the Influence of Al2O3 and CuO Nanoparticles on the Thermal Conductivity of R1234yf-Based Refrigerants
Snippet: Abstract Nano-enhanced refrigerants are substances in which the nanoparticles are suspended in the refrigerant at the desired concentration. They have the potential to improve the performance of refrigeration and air-conditioning systems that use vapour compression. This study focuses on the thermal conductivity of alumina (Al2O3) and cupric oxide (CuO) nanoparticles immersed in 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234yf). The thermal conductivity of nano-refrigerants was investigated using appropriate models from earlier studies where the volume concentration of particles and temperatures were varied from 1% to 5% and from 273 K to 323K, respectively. The acquired results are supported by prior experimental investigations on R134a-based nano-refrigerants undertaken by the researchers. The main investigation results indicate that the thermal conductivity of Al2O3/R1234yf and CuO/R1234yf is enhanced with the particle concentrations, interfacial layer thickness, and temperature. Also, the thermal conductivity of Al2O3/R1234yf and CuO/R1234yf decreases with particle size. The thermal conductivity of Al2O3/R1234yf and CuO/R1234yf nano-refrigerants become enhanced with a volume concentration of nano-sized particles by 41.2% and 148.1% respectively at 5% volume concentration and 323K temperature. The thermal conductivity of Al2O3/R1234yf reduces with temperature, by upto 3% of nanoparticle addition and after that, it enhances. Meanwhile, it declines with temperature, by upto 1% of CuO nanoparticle inclusion for CuO/R1234yf. CuO/R1234yf has a thermal conductivity of 16.69% greater than Al2O3/R1234yf at a 5% volume concentration. This paper also concludes that, among the models for thermal conductivity study, Stiprasert’s model is the most accurate and advanced.
</snippet>

Snippet: Abstract: This study explores the cutting-edge domain of nano refrigerants, aiming to boost the cooling performance of the widely used refrigerant R-134a by integrating a precisely balanced blend of CuO and SiO2 nanoparticles. The primary motivation for this research is the imperative to transform refrigeration systems, making them more energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable. The research methodology involves systematically creating a nano refrigerant by dispersing varying concentrations of CuO and SiO2 nanoparticles in R-134a. Selected for their exceptional thermal conductivity and stability, these nanoparticles have the potential to significantly enhance the heat transfer properties of the refrigerant. Initial stages encompass rigorous assessments of thermal conductivity improvements compared to the base R-134a, laying the groundwork for practical evaluations in a heat exchanger setup. In heat exchanger experiments, crucial parameters such as heat transfer coefficient, pressure drop, and overall heat transfer rate are precisely measured, providing a comprehensive understanding of the nano refrigerant’s real-world performance. The objective is not only to enhance thermal conductivity but also to optimize the nano refrigerant for effective and efficient heat exchange, thereby elevating the cooling capacity of R-134a. Stability studies are integral, ensuring the long-term viability of the nano refrigerant. Scrutinizing compatibility with commonly used refrigeration system materials and monitoring potential degradation over extended periods are essential.

- Evaporator/condenser and flow boiling: CuO consistently boosts heat‑transfer coefficients in both condensation and evaporator‑like flow boiling, often by 42–101% around 1–2% mass/volume fractions in R134a/POE systems, whereas Al2O3 yields smaller but reliable gains (tens of percent), and SiO2 can be detrimental in some flow‑boiling regimes. <cite id="2f771c58-2">At 1% mass fraction, heat‑transfer coefficient rose 42–82% and at 2% rose 50–101% in flow‑boiling with R134a/POE/CuO; condensation studies on CuO/R600a/POE reported up to ~83% maximum increase at 1.5% mass fraction</cite> <cite id="3ca389aa-2">SiO2 in R‑134a reduced heat‑transfer coefficient by up to 55% in some flow‑boiling conditions, while CuO with R134a/POE increased it by 100% in other measurements</cite>.

- Direct competition: On pure performance per dollar/charge, CuO generally “competes” harder than Al2O3, delivering larger heat‑transfer and COP gains at practical concentrations (1–2% mass/volume), but with proportionally higher penalties in viscosity/pressure drop and cost; applications that meter refrigerant/charge and can increase compressor speed or reduce evaporator/condenser sizes may favor CuO, while systems with constrained power/pressure drop budgets and rigid maintenance schedules may favor Al2O3. <cite id="2f771c58-0">R134a+CuO at 0.1–0.5% vol improved COP by 35–41% and cut power by 23% in automotive AC</cite> <cite id="2f771c58-2">CuO raised condensation heat transfer by up to ~83% at 1.5% mass fraction and boiling heat transfer by ~50–101% at 2% in flow‑boiling</cite> <cite id="758a74c1-2">Al2O3 achieved very large thermal conductivity gains at low fractions, but viscosity rises with concentration</cite>.

snippet.text: Abstract: This study explores the cutting-edge domain of nano refrigerants, aiming to boost the cooling performance of the widely used refrigerant R-134a by integrating a precisely balanced blend of CuO and SiO2 nanoparticles. The primary motivation for this research is the imperative to transform refrigeration systems, making them more energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable. The research methodology involves systematically creating a nano refrigerant by dispersing varying concentrations of CuO and SiO2 nanoparticles in R-134a. Selected for their exceptional thermal conductivity and stability, these nanoparticles have the potential to significantly enhance the heat transfer properties of the refrigerant. Initial stages encompass rigorous assessments of thermal conductivity improvements compared to the base R-134a, laying the groundwork for practical evaluations in a heat exchanger setup. In heat exchanger experiments, crucial parameters such as heat transfer coefficient, pressure drop, and overall heat transfer rate are precisely measured, providing a comprehensive understanding of the nano refrigerant’s real-world performance. The objective is not only to enhance thermal conductivity but also to optimize the nano refrigerant for effective and efficient heat exchange, thereby elevating the cooling capacity of R-134a. Stability studies are integral, ensuring the long-term viability of the nano refrigerant. Scrutinizing compatibility with commonly used refrigeration system materials and monitoring potential degradation over extended periods are essential.

Title: Metallic Oxides for Innovative Refrigerant Thermo-Physical Properties: Mathematical Models
Snippet: The thermal conductivity and the rheological behaviour of nano refrigerants based on metallic oxides were discussed. Mathematical models using different types of nanoparticles (Al2O3, CuO, SiO2, and ZnO) were used to estimate the thermo-physical properties of nano-refrigerants using a cooling unit evaporator tube. The thermal conductivity of the Al2O3/R-134a coolant was 0.0803 W/m. K at 300K temperature and 0.01 of the nanoparticles volume fractions Suspending. The fraction of refrigerant nano-particles improved thermal conductivity by around 95.96% (Al2O3/R-134a). More than 0.01 of the nanoparticles volume fractions had thermal conductivity ranging from 95.96 to 96.23 within 0.01 to 0.04 of the nanoparticles volume fractions. The viscosity of the nanorefrigerant also showed a remarkable increase of 10.75% compared to the standard refrigerant, with only 0.01 of the nanoparticles volume fractions. Volume fractions of nanoparticles and the temperature of the mixture have significant effects on the thermal conductivity and viscosity of the nanofluids. 

Results indicate that viscosity increases with the increment of the particle volume fractions. However, it decreases when the temperature increases. Nano-refrigerant density and specific heat capacity showed significant improvements in nano-particles suspended based on a volume fraction. It is essential to have the nanorefrigerant's excellent thermal properties that can withstand the variation of temperature and pressure, and the nanoparticles would probably not cause the cooling, corrosion or pressure drop in the cooling unit's efficiency.

Title: Capacities and irreversibility of the vapour compression refrigeration system’s components using aluminium oxide (Al2O3) based nanolubricants
Snippet: Mahbubul, et. al. (2013) experimentally studied the impact of nanoparticle concentration on the thermal conductivity of nanorefrigerant. 

The nanorefrigerant was prepared by dispersing Al2O3 of mean diameter 13 nm into R141b refrigerant and the concentrations considered in the analysis was varied from 0.5% to 2%. At 2% concentration, the result revealed an enhancement of 141% when compared with the base R141b refrigerant. Manasa et. al., (2021), studied the effect of nanoparticle concentration and temperature on the thermal conductivity of CuO/R600a nanorefrigerants. The thermal conductivity of nanorefrigerant was observed to increase as the temperature of the nanorefrigerant increased. This enhancement was attributed to the increase in Brownian motion. Considering the viscosity of the mixture of copper oxide (CuO) and cerium oxide (CeO2) nanoparticles dispersed in polyolester oil (POE), the viscosity increased as the concentration of CuO/CeO2 nanoparticle increased (Mohamed et. al. 2022). Mahdi et. al. (2017) reported that the viscosity of Capacities and Irreversibility of the Vapour Compression Refrigeration System's Components using Aluminium oxide (Al 2 O 3 ) based Nanolubricants 

Al2O3/R134a nanorefrigerant of nanoparticle size 20 -30 nm with a volume concentration of 0.01% and 0.02% increased as the concentration increased. An increase of 1.4% and 5.2% was obtained for 0.01% and 0.02% particle concentration, respectively. The increase in viscosity tends to affect the pumping power of the compressor and pressure drop within the VCRS. The nanoparticle size, shape, structure, and type, addition of surfactant, and temperature have significant impact on the thermophysical properties, heat transfer characteristics of the nanorefrigerants (Ali and Salam, 2020;Ogbonnaya et. al., 2020).

They have the potential to improve the performance of refrigeration and air-conditioning systems that use vapour compression. This study focuses on the thermal conductivity of alumina (Al2O3) and cupric oxide (CuO) nanoparticles immersed in 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234yf). The thermal conductivity of nano-refrigerants was investigated using appropriate models from earlier studies where the volume concentration of particles and temperatures were varied from 1% to 5% and from 273 K to 323K, respectively. The acquired results are supported by prior experimental investigations on R134a-based nano-refrigerants undertaken by the researchers. The main investigation results indicate that the thermal conductivity of Al2O3/R1234yf and CuO/R1234yf is enhanced with the particle concentrations, interfacial layer thickness, and temperature. Also, the thermal conductivity of Al2O3/R1234yf and CuO/R1234yf decreases with particle size. The thermal conductivity of Al2O3/R1234yf and CuO/R1234yf nano-refrigerants become enhanced with a volume concentration of nano-sized particles by 41.2% and 148.1% respectively at 5% volume concentration and 323K temperature. The thermal conductivity of Al2O3/R1234yf reduces with temperature, by upto 3% of nanoparticle addition and after that, it enhances. Meanwhile, it declines with temperature, by upto 1% of CuO nanoparticle inclusion for CuO/R1234yf. CuO/R1234yf has a thermal conductivity of 16.69% greater than Al2O3/R1234yf at a 5% volume concentration. This paper also concludes that, among the models for thermal conductivity study, Stiprasert’s model is the most accurate and advanced.

snippet.text:
The thermal conductivity and the rheological behaviour of nano refrigerants based on metallic oxides were discussed. Mathematical models using different types of nanoparticles (Al2O3, CuO, SiO2, and ZnO) were used to estimate the thermo-physical properties of nano-refrigerants using a cooling unit evaporator tube. The thermal conductivity of the Al2O3/R-134a coolant was 0.0803 W/m. K at 300K temperature and 0.01 of the nanoparticles volume fractions Suspending. The fraction of refrigerant nano-particles improved thermal conductivity by around 95.96% (Al2O3/R-134a). More than 0.01 of the nanoparticles volume fractions had thermal conductivity ranging from 95.96 to 96.23 within 0.01 to 0.04 of the nanoparticles volume fractions. The viscosity of the nanorefrigerant also showed a remarkable increase of 10.75% compared to the standard refrigerant, with only 0.01 of the nanoparticles volume fractions. Volume fractions of nanoparticles and the temperature of the mixture have significant effects on the thermal conductivity and viscosity of the nanofluids. 

Results indicate that viscosity increases with the increment of the particle volume fractions. However, it decreases when the temperature increases. Nano-refrigerant density and specific heat capacity showed significant improvements in nano-particles suspended based on a volume fraction. It is essential to have the nanorefrigerant's excellent thermal properties that can withstand the variation of temperature and pressure, and the nanoparticles would probably not cause the cooling, corrosion or pressure drop in the cooling unit's efficiency.

Mahbubul, et. al. (2013) experimentally studied the impact of nanoparticle concentration on the thermal conductivity of nanorefrigerant. 

The nanorefrigerant was prepared by dispersing Al2O3 of mean diameter 13 nm into R141b refrigerant and the concentrations considered in the analysis was varied from 0.5% to 2%. At 2% concentration, the result revealed an enhancement of 141% when compared with the base R141b refrigerant. Manasa et. al., (2021), studied the effect of nanoparticle concentration and temperature on the thermal conductivity of CuO/R600a nanorefrigerants. The thermal conductivity of nanorefrigerant was observed to increase as the temperature of the nanorefrigerant increased. This enhancement was attributed to the increase in Brownian motion. Considering the viscosity of the mixture of copper oxide (CuO) and cerium oxide (CeO2) nanoparticles dispersed in polyolester oil (POE), the viscosity increased as the concentration of CuO/CeO2 nanoparticle increased (Mohamed et. al. 2022). Mahdi et. al. (2017) reported that the viscosity of Capacities and Irreversibility of the Vapour Compression Refrigeration System's Components using Aluminium oxide (Al 2 O 3 ) based Nanolubricants 

Al2O3/R134a nanorefrigerant of nanoparticle size 20 -30 nm with a volume concentration of 0.01% and 0.02% increased as the concentration increased. An increase of 1.4% and 5.2% was obtained for 0.01% and 0.02% particle concentration, respectively. The increase in viscosity tends to affect the pumping power of the compressor and pressure drop within the VCRS. The nanoparticle size, shape, structure, and type, addition of surfactant, and temperature have significant impact on the thermophysical properties, heat transfer characteristics of the nanorefrigerants (Ali and Salam, 2020;Ogbonnaya et. al., 2020).

snippet.text:
Numerical tests have been carried out for 4 types of nanoparticles, namely Al2O3, CuO, SiO2, and ZnO, with a diameter of 30 nm and a volumetric concentration of 5%. These nanoparticles were dispersed in several hydrocarbon-based refrigerants, namely tetrafluoromethane (R134a), propane (R290), butane (R600), isobutane (R600a), and propylene (R1270). The results showed that propylene had the best heat transfer and pressure drop characteristics among all the hydrocarbon refrigerants tested. CuO as nanoparticles and a volumetric concentration of 5% were the most suitable due to their high thermal and fluid characteristics. 

In this paper, Kanthimathi T. et al. [15] investigated the heat transfer coefficient of nano refrigerants based on the different volume concentrations of Al2O3 nanoparticles suspended in R134a. The correlations from the existing studies have been used to determine the thermophysical properties such as thermal conduction, viscosity, density, and specific heat of nano-refrigerants. The results showed that the heat transfer coefficient will also increase by increasing the volume concentration of nano refrigerants. 

Soheel A.H. et al. [16] This paper presents a numerical investigation and comparison of heat transfer coefficients for eco-friendly refrigerants R134a and R600a with Al2O3 and TiO2 nanoparticles at concentrations of 1, 2, 3, and 4%. The numerical investigation was simulated with a CFD model using ANSYS FLUENT 14.5 software. The results showed that higher heat transfer coefficients increased with increasing concentration of nanoparticles. R134a+TiO2 nano refrigerant is an excellent nano refrigerant in vapor compression systems because it has higher heat transfer coefficients than other nano refrigerants.

Addition of nanoparticles to refrigerants and lubricants improves thermal characteristics and lowers power wastage. In this paper R134a refrigerant is added with nanoparticle CuO in the concentration of 0.1%v to 0.5%v and its performance is evaluated. Title: "Advanced Materials in Refrigeration Systems: An In-depth Analysis of Novel Additives and Their Influence on Heat Transfer Efficiency and Energy Consumption"
Snippet: Abstract: This study explores the cutting-edge domain of nano refrigerants, aiming to boost the cooling performance of the widely used refrigerant R-134a by integrating a precisely balanced blend of CuO and SiO2 nanoparticles. The primary motivation for this research is the imperative to transform refrigeration systems, making them more energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable. The research methodology involves systematically creating a nano refrigerant by dispersing varying concentrations of CuO and SiO2 nanoparticles in R-134a. Selected for their exceptional thermal conductivity and stability, these nanoparticles have the potential to significantly enhance the heat transfer properties of the refrigerant. Initial stages encompass rigorous assessments of thermal conductivity improvements compared to the base R-134a, laying the groundwork for practical evaluations in a heat exchanger setup. In heat exchanger experiments, crucial parameters such as heat transfer coefficient, pressure drop, and overall heat transfer rate are precisely measured, providing a comprehensive understanding of the nano refrigerant’s real-world performance. The objective is not only to enhance thermal conductivity but also to optimize the nano refrigerant for effective and efficient heat exchange, thereby elevating the cooling capacity of R-134a. Stability studies are integral, ensuring the long-term viability of the nano refrigerant. Scrutinizing compatibility with commonly used refrigeration system materials and monitoring potential degradation over extended periods are essential.

Title: Experimental study of a domestic refrigerator using (SiO 2 /PAG oil/R- 134a) nano-refrigerant as a replacement for pure R-134a
Snippet: It was found that the use of a nano-refrigerant was both ecologically friendly and safe. Kristen Bartelt et al [6] investigated the CuO nano-particles to see how they affect the flow-boiling of an (R134a/POE oil) mixture in a plane tube. Along with synthetic-ester and copper oxide nano-particles dissolved in the mix at 4% concentration. The heat-transfer coefficient improved by 42 to 82 % when utilizing a nano-lubricant mass fraction of 1% compared to a refrigerant-oil combination that without nanoparticles. When the mass fraction was increased to 2%, the heat-transfer coefficient enhanced by 50% to 101 %. Gill et al [7] investigated the energy and exergy characteristic of a household refrigeration system. Employing R134a, and the Liquefied Petroleum Gas refrigerants with various oils (Polyester, Mineral oil, and TiO₂, SiO₂, and Al₂O₃ nanoparticles dispersed in mineral oil). Among the evaluated nano-lubricants, the household refrigerator employing LPG refrigerant at 40 g charge with TiO2-MO (0.2 g/L TiO2) lubricant exhibited the greatest COP and second lowest efficiency (56.32 % and 47.06 %, respectively, greater than R134a/POE). With the least energy and exergy performance analysis of the domestic refrigerator. Henderson et al [8] quantified the effect of using nanoparticles like SiO₂/CuO on the flow-boiling of pure R134a and R134a/POE-oil mixes throughout mass-fluxes between 100 kg/m²s and 400 kg/m²s. The results showed using SiO₂ nanoparticles with R-134a, the heat-transfer coefficient decreased by up to 55 %. When CuO nanoparticles were utilized with an R-134a/Polyester mixture, the heat-transfer coefficient rose by 100 %.

Thus, it can be concluded that R290/R600a mixture could be an ozone-friendly, energy efficient, and safe viable alternative to R134a for domestic refrigeration systems. 

Evaporating heat transfer is very important in the refrigeration and air-conditioning systems. HFC 134a is the mostly widely used alternative refrigerant in refrigeration equipment such as domestic refrigerators and air conditioners. Coumaressin (2014) investigated the effect of using CuO-R134a in the vapour compression system on the evaporating heat transfer coefficient. Based on the applications, nanoparticles are currently made out of a very wide variety of materials, the most common of the new generation of nanoparticles being ceramics, which are best split into metal oxide ceramics, such as titanium, zinc, aluminium and iron oxides, to name a prominent few and silicate nanoparticles, generally in the form of Nano scale flakes of clay. Nano refrigerant is nothing but the combination of Nano particle to the refrigerant for the sake of better refrigeration process. By addition of nanoparticles to the refrigerant results in improvements in the thermo physical properties and heat transfer characteristics of the refrigerant, thereby improving the performance of the refrigeration system. CuO nanoparticle with R134a refrigerant can be used as an excellent refrigerant to improve the heat transfer characteristics in a refrigeration system. The obtained evaporating heat transfer coefficient result with increases with the usage of Nano CuO. The Nano particles like AL2O3, CuO and TiO2. Now can be form some other Nano refrigerant by combining the different Nano particles of same size. The most common refrigerant in current time is R132a in all the refrigeration systems like vapour compression refrigeration system, domestic refrigerators and air conditioners.

Title: Evaluation of a Refrigeration System Based on Nano-Refrigerants and Nano-Lubricants
Snippet: Nagaraju and Reddy (2018) evaluated the performance of VCRs based on nano-refrigerants consisting of 0.05 to 0.8 wt.% of CuO particle size range 10 to 70 nm is dispersed into R134a. The results showed that 0.8 wt.% of CuO was the optimal concentration which achieved the highest heat transfer enhancement, enhanced COP and reduction of power consumption, but the cost of nano-refrigerant was expensive (Nagaraju and Reddy, 2018). Kumar and Tiwari (2019) evaluated the performance of VCRs based on R134a/PAG oil, R600a/PAG oil and Cu nanoparticles is dispersed into R600a. The results showed that R600a achieved a higher COP and refrigeration effect around 27.12% and 25% respectively as compare to R134a, while the reduction of power consumption was 1.69 % which was less than that of R134a. Moreover dispersing 0.5 wt. %, 1wt % and 1.5 wt.% of Cu into R600a improved COP, refrigeration effect and reduced the power consumption as compared to pure R600a (Kumar and Tiwari, 2019). Kumar et al. (2016) investigated the performance of VCRs based on 0.01 vol% and 0.06 vol % of ZrO2, particle size diameter 20 nm is dispersed into both R134a and R152a. The results indicated that the improvement of COP was 33.45% based on (0.06 vol % of ZrO2 -R152a) nanorefrigerant. The application of R152a as a refrigerant was environmentally beneficial due to its properties such as zero ozone depletion potential and very low global worming potential (Kumar et al., 2016). Mahdi et al. (2017) evaluated the performance of VCRs based on nano-refrigerant consisting of 0.01vol % and 0.02 vol% of Al2O3, diameter size of 20-30 nm was dispersed into R134a.

snippet.text: Nagaraju and Reddy (2018) evaluated the performance of VCRs based on nano-refrigerants consisting of 0.05 to 0.8 wt.% of CuO particle size range 10 to 70 nm is dispersed into R134a. The results showed that 0.8 wt.% of CuO was the optimal concentration which achieved the highest heat transfer enhancement, enhanced COP and reduction of power consumption, but the cost of nano-refrigerant was expensive (Nagaraju and Reddy, 2018). Kumar and Tiwari (2019) evaluated the performance of VCRs based on R134a/PAG oil, R600a/PAG oil and Cu nanoparticles is dispersed into R600a. The results showed that R600a achieved a higher COP and refrigeration effect around 27.12% and 25% respectively as compare to R134a, while the reduction of power consumption was 1.69 % which was less than that of R134a. Moreover dispersing 0.5 wt. %, 1wt % and 1.5 wt.% of Cu into R600a improved COP, refrigeration effect and reduced the power consumption as compared to pure R600a (Kumar and Tiwari, 2019). Kumar et al. (2016) investigated the performance of VCRs based on 0.01 vol% and 0.06 vol % of ZrO2, particle size diameter 20 nm is dispersed into both R134a and R152a. The results indicated that the improvement of COP was 33.45% based on (0.06 vol % of ZrO2 -R152a) nanorefrigerant. The application of R152a as a refrigerant was environmentally beneficial due to its properties such as zero ozone depletion potential and very low global worming potential (Kumar et al., 2016). Mahdi et al. (2017) evaluated the performance of VCRs based on nano-refrigerant consisting of 0.01vol % and 0.02 vol% of Al2O3, diameter size of 20-30 nm was dispersed into R134a.

documents.title: "Advanced Materials in Refrigeration Systems: An In-depth Analysis of Novel Additives and Their Influence on Heat Transfer Efficiency and Energy Consumption"
documents.snippet: Abstract: This study explores the cutting-edge domain of nano refrigerants, aiming to boost the cooling performance of the widely used refrigerant R-134a by integrating a precisely balanced blend of CuO and SiO2 nanoparticles. The primary motivation for this research is the imperative to transform refrigeration systems, making them more energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable. The research methodology involves systematically creating a nano refrigerant by dispersing varying concentrations of CuO and SiO2 nanoparticles in R-134a. Selected for their exceptional thermal conductivity and stability, these nanoparticles have the potential to significantly enhance the heat transfer properties of the refrigerant. Initial stages encompass rigorous assessments of thermal conductivity improvements compared to the base R-134a, laying the groundwork for practical evaluations in a heat exchanger setup. In heat exchanger experiments, crucial parameters such as heat transfer coefficient, pressure drop, and overall heat transfer rate are precisely measured, providing a comprehensive understanding of the nano refrigerant’s real-world performance. The objective is not only to enhance thermal conductivity but also to optimize the nano refrigerant for effective and efficient heat exchange, thereby elevating the cooling capacity of R-134a. Stability studies are integral, ensuring the long-term viability of the nano refrigerant. Scrutinizing compatibility with commonly used refrigeration system materials and monitoring potential degradation over extended periods are essential.
